A0113.title: IoT Traffic Anomaly Detection and C&C Communication Blocking
A0113.definition: Using machine learning models to detect abnormal network behavior in IoT devices, and identifying and blocking botnet C&C (Command and Control) communication.
A0113.description: Botnets rely on C&C servers to issue commands, and severing this communication can disrupt attacks. Detection methods: using machine learning to analyze device traffic characteristics and identify botnet features such as DGA domains, abnormal DNS queries, and non-standard port communication; deploying Deep Packet Inspection (DPI) at the gateway to identify known botnet protocols (e.g., Mirai variants); monitoring for sudden large-scale outbound connections and scanning behavior; establishing a baseline of normal traffic and triggering alerts upon deviation. Blocking measures: DNS filtering to block known C&C domains; firewall rules to restrict devices to whitelisted services only; automatically isolating infected devices upon detection.
A0113.limitation: Machine learning models require large amounts of training data and are prone to false positives; emerging botnets may use encrypted communication to evade detection; DGA domains are generated rapidly, making real-time blacklist updates difficult; limited effectiveness in detecting encrypted traffic.
keywords: IoT Traffic Anomaly Detection and C&C Communication Blocking

A0113-001.title: IoT Traffic Monitoring and Anomaly Detection
A0113-001.description: Monitors IoT device network traffic to detect anomalous external connections by capturing signals such as network flows, outbound connections, DNS queries, and port communications. A normal traffic baseline is established, and machine learning models combined with rule-based matching are used to identify abnormal behaviors including DGA domains, non-standard ports, and scanning outbound connections, triggering alerts when deviations from the baseline occur.
keywords: IoT Traffic Monitoring and Anomaly Detection
A0113-001.definition: Monitor IoT device network traffic to detect abnormal outbound connections.
A0113-001.limitation: Emerging botnets may use encrypted communication, protocol-layer forgery, or rapidly mutating DGA domains to evade detection, limiting the effectiveness of DPI under encrypted traffic. Normal firmware updates and OTA polling can be easily confused with C&C outbound connections, leading to false positives. The large number of IoT devices also makes it difficult to maintain a stable baseline.
